question.prompt: Six chairs are arranged around a round table. Two students and two teachers randomly select four of the chairs to sit in. What is the probability that the two students will sit in two adjacent chairs and the two teachers will also sit in two adjacent chairs?

solutions.title: Condition on the students sitting together
solutions.explanation:
When the students occupy adjacent chairs, the four remaining chairs form one consecutive run. This makes the teachers' adjacent pairs easy to count.

Seat the students first. After the first student sits down, the second student has five equally likely chairs to choose from. Exactly two are adjacent to the first student's chair, so the probability of student adjacency is \(\frac25\).

Given that the students sit together, label the four remaining chairs \(1,2,3,4\) consecutively along the unoccupied run. The teachers can occupy any of
\[
\binom42=\frac{4\cdot3}{2}=6
\]
pairs. These pairs are equally likely because each allows two assignments of the teachers. Exactly three pairs are adjacent: \(\{1,2\}\), \(\{2,3\}\), and \(\{3,4\}\).

Multiplying the probability of student adjacency by the conditional probability of teacher adjacency gives
\[
\frac25\cdot\frac36=\boxed{\frac15}.
\]
The answer is choice B.
